items.title: Financial Fragility in Societies of LLM Agents: Coordination Failures and Stabilizing Mechanisms
items.one_liner: Design multi-agent financial systems with early, centralized commitment mechanisms to prevent cascading coordination failures and bank runs.
items.summary: Researchers studied systemic financial fragility caused by interacting large language model agents using FRAIL, a controlled experimental framework modeling bank runs, debt rollover, and reward crowdfunding. Across seven leading LLMs, baseline episodes exhibited widespread collective failure—77 percent of bank runs and 83 percent of debt rollovers collapsed even without any malicious or destabilizing instructions given to agents. Testing three mitigation mechanisms based on compensated commitments, centralized agreements, and participant coalitions showed that all improved aggregate outcomes but did not universally excel. Successful stabilization consistently relied on early, broad-based commitments formed before defensive behaviors became self-reinforcing.
items.bottom_line: LLM agents acting individually can create highly fragile financial systems prone to catastrophic coordination collapse unless bound by early commitments.

items.one_liner: T-RoPE improves sequential recommendation accuracy by incorporating temporal awareness into the Transformer architecture, outperforming standard index-based embeddings.

items.summary: Kaspersky ICS CERT published an advisory regarding a local privilege escalation vulnerability in Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk Activation Manager affecting all versions prior to V5.03. By hijacking the resulting console host window and launching a third-party system-wide web browser (such as Mozilla Firefox or Google Chrome), an attacker can open an elevated command prompt. Rockwell Automation has released V5.03 to fix the issue, while mitigations include Microsoft AppLocker configurations and avoiding system-wide third-party web browsers.

items.title: Externalized CPDAG Summaries Improve LLM Causal Deduction
items.one_liner: Structured Thinking uses schema-constrained CPDAG summaries to significantly boost LLM causal reasoning performance.
items.summary: To address how causal claims hold in DAGs, researchers propose Structured Thinking, a two-turn pipeline that externalizes a typed, schema-constrained CPDAG summary before answering against that graph state. On the Corr2Cause full test, this pipeline raises Qwen3.5-27B from 73.0 to 86.4 F1(Yes) over a PC-instruction baseline. Scrambling the emitted CPDAG costs 12.0 pp F1, and a full-split audit shows close agreement with the reference CPDAG. The findings suggest that externalizing the latent object defining the label and constraining its form significantly improves LLM causal deduction.
items.bottom_line: Externalizing schema-constrained latent objects like CPDAG summaries enables LLMs to perform complex causal deduction far more reliably.
